_comment: Config for the in-page correction requests.
Field ids were read out of a 'Get pre-filled link' URL. To change the
form, repeat that: fill each question with a recognisable dummy value,
copy the generated URL, and update the ids below.
Google Form was chosen over GitHub Issues deliberately: a GitHub account
is a hard wall for most residents, and public engagement is the point.
If volume ever justifies it, a Cloudflare Worker writing to the repo via
the GitHub API removes the third party entirely -- and comes free if the
site moves to Cloudflare Pages for the Phase 3.2 wildcard redirects.
EVERY field is prefilled, including the two the contributor edits:
timestamp  -- prefilled with the original; edit it to fix bad timing.
The untouched original is still recoverable from page_url
(#t=), so nothing is lost by making this field editable.
suggestion -- prefilled with the ORIGINAL TEXT, so a fix is a quick edit
rather than retyping a sentence.
Worth relabelling those two questions in the form to match, e.g.
'Timestamp in seconds (edit if the timing is wrong)' and
'Corrected text (edit the text below)'.
NOTE on the two SPEAKER_00 fields in the source URL: both the speaker
label and the original text were filled with the same dummy value, so
they were told apart by their ORDER in the prefill URL, which follows
question order. If 'speaker' and 'original_text' arrive swapped in the
responses sheet, exchange entry.190036418 and entry.28606286 below.
ANONYMIZATION IS CURRENTLY OFF. The option was removed pending a decision
on policy and on how requests would actually be fulfilled (a private
real-name -> pseudonym mapping, render-time substitution, a review queue,
and the unmasking rule for candidates). anonymize_notice is kept below so
re-enabling is just restoring the 'anonymize' entry under kinds -- but do
not restore it before there is a process behind it, because the menu is a
public promise. See plan.txt.
NOTHING here is secret; this file is public config. The private
real-name -> pseudonym mapping must NEVER live here.
anonymize_notice: Anonymization is offered to members of the public, not to elected officials, candidates for office, or city staff speaking in their official capacity. If you later run for or hold public office, your name will be restored across the archive so that candidates remain accountable for their public statements. We can remove your name from this site, but not from the city's own published video.
